title: Hold memory/storage configuration (knob_changes=[]): WAL, checkpoint, bgwriter and host-I/O telemetry show no queued storage mechanism, the 'wal_wait' alert is a single-sample artifact, and the terminal-dominant transaction is read-only
why_exceeds_incumbent: It does not claim to exceed the incumbent and deliberately does not perturb it: every storage-relevant signal sits at the noise floor (30.4 ms of WAL device-write per second, 0.0 host_io stall, 0 checkpoint write/sync time, 0 buffers_clean/s, 0 temp bytes, 0.99992 buffer hit ratio) and the single wal_wait sample is uncorroborated by wal_timing, wait events and host_io read together. Spending a measurement on an unsupported storage knob would move nothing and would risk a real regression, for example lowering commit_siblings below the observed sibling count would activate the incumbent's 671 us commit_delay on every commit. The value delivered is refuting the high-severity wal_wait alert with three independent signals and redirecting the next measurement to the only lever that matters, the read-only GetUserTweets executor path already holding 0.881 of terminal capacity.

alternatives.statement: The GetUserTweets tail is caused by heavyweight row/relation lock waits on the writer path (InsertTweet) blocking the dominant read class, so a lock-sizing knob should relieve it.
A genuine WAL flush stall (the wal_wait alert) serializes the commit path and spills into the reader tail, so wal_writer/commit knobs should relieve it.
Autovacuum/autoanalyze on a growing heap contends for buffers and I/O with the read class, so aggressive autovacuum knobs should relieve it.

The read tail is lightweight-lock contention (buffer-mapping / ProcArray / snapshot LWLock) that heavyweight lock metrics cannot see, so it would require session/connection-level concurrency changes rather than loud lock waits.
